patch_description: Crossover of the baseline per-destination Dijkstra approach (Program 1: robust, simple, guaranteed success) and the current greedy Steiner-tree approach (lowest cost, 756.69). The new program keeps the shared-backbone strategy that made the current program cheapest: destinations are processed greedily, and any edge already in the multicast tree is heavily discounted so subsequent destinations reuse existing transfers instead of paying for redundant parallel links. It retains the cost backfilling (None -> large finite penalty) and explicit reachability checks from the current program for robustness, plus the random perturbation restarts that occasionally find cheaper tree hook-ins. The deterministic Steiner-style tree from Program 2 is blended in by first ordering destinations by their plain Dijkstra cost (cheapest first), which grows the backbone toward nearby nodes before attaching far ones — empirically improving shared-edge reuse. Output format (BroadCastTopology with per-dst per-partition edge lists) is unchanged.
